Legion Contain — drill card

Setup: Mark a 10–15-yard long area with cones. One ball carrier, two defenders; remaining players queue and rotate. Begin at walking/jogging speed.

Execution: The runner advances toward the finish line. D1 closes under control and targets the near-side flag; D2 protects the cutback/escape lane. No pushing, blocking, grabbing clothing, or body contact. Rotate every repetition.

Unit 01

Offense

Compact concept-based football: create conflict, play on time, develop every player and manufacture yards after catch.

Offensive Philosophy

Protect simplicity.
Six core pass concepts become automatic before the menu expands.
Play on time.
Train 2–3 second decisions even with the seven-second NFL FLAG ceiling.
Create conflict.
Every concept should place a defender in a two-choice problem.
Everyone develops.
Centers catch, runners run routes, receivers handle the ball, and multiple players train as passers.
YAC matters.
Prefer accurate short throws over low-percentage hero balls.
Space legally.
No blocking or picks. Routes and leverage create separation.

Rules That Shape the Offense

QB cannot run across the LOS
QB run concepts require a legal backward exchange first.
Forward pass must cross the LOS
No behind-LOS forward screens; flats must be caught beyond the line.
7-second pass clock
Base offense targets a decision in 2–3 seconds.
Backward exchange
Unlocks run/pass packages, but then every defender may rush.
No-run zones
Use the RED menu. Completion must satisfy the pass requirement.
1–2 designated rushers
QB identifies rush posture before the snap and plays on rhythm.

Route Standards

RouteLandmark / Standard
FlatGain width quickly; catch beyond LOS; square shoulders after catch.
Slant3 hard steps, plant outside foot, cross defender’s face at ~45°.
StickPush 5–6 yards; settle away from leverage or break out if tagged.
Drag / MeshShallow 3–5 yards; maintain spacing; run vs man, settle only when coached vs zone.
OutVertical stem first; sharp 90° break; ball on outside shoulder.
CornerStem inside leverage; break 45° to open grass.
PostVertical stem; attack safety leverage; break to middle.
GoStack defender; late hands; stay on line unless tagged.
SitFind open zone window beyond LOS; show numbers to QB.

QB Operating System

Situation
Down, line-to-gain, RED, score and time.
Numbers
Where does the defense have extra bodies?
Leverage
Inside/outside? Press/off? Safety help?
Rush
0, 1 or 2 declared rushers?
Key
Which defender does the concept put in conflict?
Progression
Read the concept, not a favorite receiver.
Ball placement
Throw away from leverage and protect the receiver.

12

Slant / Flat

Spread · Quick Game

QB Read

Key the flat defender. If he widens, throw the slant. If he squeezes, throw the flat.

Assignments

  • X: backside clear/tagged slant
  • Y: slant, win inside leverage
  • C: sit beyond LOS
  • Z: flat beyond LOS
  • Q: key flat defender, deliver on rhythm

Why We Carry It

Teaches leverage, timing, and defender conflict.

11

Stick

Spread · Quick Game

QB Read

Read the outside underneath defender. Widens = Stick. Sits inside = flat/out.

Assignments

  • X: clear/go or backside access
  • Y: Stick at 5-6, settle away from leverage
  • C: middle sit/seam by tag
  • Z: flat/out beyond LOS
  • Q: read Stick-side leverage

Why We Carry It

Simple zone answer that develops anticipation and leverage recognition.

21

Mesh

Spread · Man / Spacing

QB Read

Identify man vs. zone. Against man, lead the crosser away from leverage; against zone, use the center sit/window.

Assignments

  • X: shallow cross 3-5
  • Y: opposite shallow cross, stagger depth
  • C: sit/hook beyond LOS
  • Z: clear/post or wheel tag
  • Q: man = lead runner; zone = settle/window

Why We Carry It

Primary man-beater; teaches spacing, communication, and route recognition.

32

Flood

Trips Right · Zone Stretch

QB Read

Read the sideline structure high-to-low while preserving three distinct levels.

Assignments

  • X: backside clear/alert
  • C: short out/flat beyond LOS
  • Y: intermediate corner/out
  • Z: deep clear/go
  • Q: high -> intermediate -> short

Why We Carry It

Classic three-level stretch that transfers directly to tackle passing concepts.

31

Smash

Spread · High / Low

QB Read

If the corner defender squats, throw the corner. If he sinks, take the hitch/out.

Assignments

  • X: hitch/out at 5-6
  • Y: corner behind X
  • C: middle control/sit
  • Z: backside hitch or tagged go
  • Q: high-low the corner defender

Why We Carry It

Teaches a clean high-low read and anticipation.

41

Verticals

Spread · Vertical

QB Read

Pre-snap identify matchup and safety leverage. If nothing is clean, use the center control route.

Assignments

  • X: go
  • Y: seam/go
  • C: middle seam/sit by call
  • Z: go
  • Q: pre-snap leverage, post-snap safety position

Why We Carry It

Develops ball tracking, vertical releases, and safety recognition.

51

Jet

Spread · Action / Run

QB Read

Backward exchange behind the LOS; timing must be fast because all defenders can then cross the LOS.

Assignments

  • X: clear space legally
  • Y: inside clear
  • C: release opposite
  • Z: Jet motion, backward exchange, attack edge
  • Q: secure snap, exchange, carry fake

Why We Carry It

Develops ball handling, pursuit recognition, and open-field running.

52

Jet Counter

Spread · Action / Run

QB Read

Use after the defense overplays Jet flow. Show the same picture, then attack vacated space.

Assignments

  • X: clear opposite
  • Y: sell flow, occupy space legally
  • C: release opposite
  • Z: sell Jet, counter after exchange
  • Q: identical Jet mechanics

Why We Carry It

Punishes pursuit while teaching flow and cutback responsibility.

53

Jet Pass

Spread · Action / Pass

QB Read

After the backward exchange, Z becomes the passer and the original QB becomes eligible. Make a fast high-to-low read.

Assignments

  • X: deep/post alert
  • Y: intermediate cross
  • C: short sit beyond LOS
  • Z: Jet motion, exchange, passer
  • Q: sell exchange, release as receiver

Why We Carry It

Creates multiplicity while developing a second passer.

61

Red Stick

Trips Right · RED / No-Run

QB Read

PASS REQUIRED. Same Stick rules with compressed landmarks; every catch must be beyond the LOS.

Assignments

  • X: backside slant/clear
  • C: short sit beyond LOS
  • Y: Stick beyond LOS
  • Z: flat/out beyond LOS
  • Q: fast leverage read

Why We Carry It

Tiny, highly rehearsed no-run-zone answer.

RED / Goal-Line Menu

RED means pass mandatory. Keep the menu tiny and rehearsed: 61 Red Stick first, then add compressed Mesh and Flood only after the base concepts are automatic. Every player must know the line-to-gain and goal line before the snap.

90-Series Specials

CallConceptSetup
91 Jet ThrowbackJet action → original QB/backsideAfter defenders aggressively flow to Jet.
92 Mesh WheelBase Mesh + tagged wheelAfter defenders chase crossers horizontally.
93 Flood ReturnFlood presentation + backside returnAfter zone over-rotates to Trips.
94 Double PassBackward exchange → legal forward passOnly with a trained secondary passer.

Unit 02

Defense

Protect the deep ball. Eliminate free yards. Pull flags in space. Make the quarterback hold the football.

D1 LOCK
D2 SHELL
D3 SKY
D4 HAWK
D5 FIRE
D6 RED

Defensive Philosophy

No Explosives
Make the offense complete multiple throws. A short catch with an immediate flag pull is a defensive win.
Rally & Pull
First defender controls leverage; second defender hunts the flag. Never turn a missed flag into a touchdown.
Pressure With Purpose
A rusher compresses time while maintaining a controlled path and avoiding illegal contact.
Communicate
Build OUT, IN, CROSS, SWITCH, DEEP and BALL into every practice.
Develop Everyone
Every player learns coverage, pursuit, route recognition, flag pulling and basic rush technique.

NFL FLAG Rules That Drive Our Defense

Up to two rushers
Rushers identify and begin from at least seven yards.
Immediate rush
An identified legal rusher must rush immediately; no delayed rush.
Backward exchange
After a handoff, pitch or backward lateral behind the LOS, every defender may cross the LOS.
Free releases
No grabbing, rerouting, blocking or illegal contact with receivers.
Flag pull, not tackle
Defenders may dive for a flag but cannot tackle, hold or run through the carrier.
Seven-second clock
The defense is not required to rush while the normal pass clock is active.

Flag Pulling & Pursuit

StepStandard
Track the near hipThe hip tells you where the runner is going; do not stare at the flag.
Break downShorten stride, stay square and arrive under control.
LeverageForce the runner toward help or the sideline; remove the cutback.
Pull throughAttack the flag with the near hand and pull through the belt line.
RallyIf you miss, turn and pursue immediately. No spectators.
D1

LOCK - MAN

BASE | PRESSURE FRIENDLY | SIMPLE

Play Overview

Our simplest answer when matchups are favorable. Four defenders play man while one designated rusher accelerates the quarterback clock.

Responsibilities

  • CBL — X man; inside leverage unless formation or sideline changes it.
  • M — C man; expect quick sit, drag and seam.
  • N — Y man; deny the easy inside release.
  • CBR — Z man; protect vertical first.
  • R — Declare rush, attack under control and contain the escape lane.

Coaching Points

  • Eyes on your man, not the quarterback.
  • Stay square through the release; no grabbing or rerouting.
  • Trail the hip on crossers and communicate traffic.
  • Nearest defender attacks the flag; next defender becomes leverage/pursuit.

When To Call It

Favorable matchups · Need pressure without sacrificing structure · Opponent living on quick timing routes

D2

SHELL - COVER 2

ZONE | FLAT CONTROL | RED-ZONE FRIENDLY

Play Overview

Our primary zone structure. Two deep defenders protect verticals while three underneath defenders squeeze quick game and rally to flags.

Responsibilities

  • S1 / S2 — Own deep half; midpoint vertical threats and never get beaten over the top.
  • F1 / F2 — Flat/curl defenders; expand with routes and rally downhill.
  • H — Hook/middle; read QB, close windows and pass crossers through zones.

Coaching Points

  • Keep everything in front.
  • Zone eyes: see the QB through the receiver.
  • Communicate IN / OUT / CROSS.
  • Break on the throw, not the pump fake.

When To Call It

Base zone call · Balanced spread teams · Red-zone / pass-first situations

D3

SKY - COVER 3

ZONE | 3 DEEP | CROSSER CONTROL

Play Overview

Useful against teams that want verticals, corners and deep crossers. It forces patient underneath completions and creates rally opportunities.

Responsibilities

  • D1 / D2 / D3 — Stay on top of vertical threats and overlap seams.
  • U1 / U2 — Split underneath space, carry crossers until passed, then rally.

Coaching Points

  • No defender lets a receiver get behind him.
  • Under defenders close throwing lanes without chasing ghosts.
  • Deep defenders communicate vertical exchanges early.

When To Call It

Opponent attacking deep · Protecting a lead · Need eyes on QB and rally tackling

D4

HAWK - 1 RUSH MATCH

MATCH | DISGUISE | BASE PRESSURE

Play Overview

A developmental bridge between zone and man. Defenders begin in zone landmarks but match receivers entering their responsibility.

Responsibilities

  • Outside defenders — Match the first outside threat.
  • Inside defenders — Match the first inside threat and communicate crossers.
  • H — Declare rush and compress the QB launch point.

Coaching Points

  • Do not chase motion blindly; communicate the new threat.
  • Match verticals aggressively; pass shallow crossers when called.
  • Rush and coverage must work together.

When To Call It

Zone disguise with man-like matching · Motion/crossers · Need one rusher to speed the QB

D5

FIRE - 2 RUSH

PRESSURE | FAST CLOCK | SITUATIONAL

Play Overview

Our change-up pressure. Two legal rushers force an immediate answer while three defenders protect the most dangerous receiving space.

Responsibilities

  • R1 / R2 — Both identify at seven yards and rush immediately; maintain separate lanes.
  • C1 / C2 — Outside leverage with eyes through threats.
  • S — Deep middle; erase seams, posts and busted coverage.

Coaching Points

  • Use selectively; pressure creates open space.
  • Rushers cannot make avoidable contact with the QB.
  • Coverage must expect hot throws immediately.

When To Call It

Long yardage / must-have stop · QB holding the ball · Change-up after showing single rush

D6

RED - GOAL LINE

PASS-FIRST | NO-RUN ZONE | TIGHT SPACE

Play Overview

A compressed-field package for the five-yard no-run zone and one-point PATs, where the offense must use a forward pass across the LOS.

Responsibilities

  • Outside — Protect quick outs/corners and drive on throws.
  • Inside — Take away slants, sticks and mesh windows.
  • S — Own the back line and overlap every vertical release.

Coaching Points

  • Depth shrinks with the field; do not retreat into the end line.
  • Expect rub concepts; avoid collisions and communicate switches.
  • Hands off receivers: free releases are required.

When To Call It

Inside 5-yard no-run zone · 1-point PAT · Compressed field / bunch and mesh teams

Defensive Situational Call Sheet

SituationStarting Point
Normal fieldD2 Shell or D4 Hawk; use D1 Lock when matchups are favorable.
Long yardageD3 Sky protects verticals; D5 Fire is the pressure change-up.
No-run / goal lineD6 Red. Compress windows and communicate switches.
After backward exchangeAll defenders may cross the LOS. Nearest defender attacks the new ball carrier/passer while others preserve leverage until run/pass declares.
Protecting a leadFavor D3 Sky and D2 Shell. Force the offense to execute underneath repeatedly.
Need a turnoverPressure selectively without abandoning leverage. Transition immediately after an interception.

WeekEmphasis

3D2 Shell — Cover 2 spacing
4D3 Sky — Cover 3 spacing
5D4 Hawk — match communication
6D5 Fire — two-rush pressure
7D6 Red — no-run / goal-line defense

Defensive standard: NO FREE YARDS. NO EXPLOSIVES. FIVE HATS TO THE FLAG.

Core Drill Library

A. Partner Catch Ladder

  • 5 stationary chest
  • 5 outside-right
  • 5 outside-left
  • 5 moving right
  • 5 moving left
  • Coach cue: eyes-through-hands, tuck, accelerate.

B. Route Break Box

  • Four cones make 5-yard stem box.
  • Player bursts vertical, sinks hips, makes 45/90-degree break.
  • Coach cue: no drifting, no rounded corners.

C. Near-Hip Flag Pull

  • Ball carrier jogs 5-7 yards through channel.
  • Defender closes under control, eyes near hip, grabs flag and freezes.
  • Progress speed from 50% to game speed.

D. Pursuit Triangle

  • Ball carrier chooses left/right lane.
  • First defender maintains leverage; second defender tracks inside-out.
  • Score clean flag pull without overrun.

E. 7-Yard Rush Timer

  • Rusher starts legal 7 yards away.
  • Time first movement to controlled arrival near QB landmark.
  • Do not reward reckless contact.

F. QB Quick Clock

  • Coach starts timer at snap.
  • QB must complete read and throw by 3.0 seconds on quick concepts.
  • Grade decision and placement, not completion alone.

G. 2v2 Conflict

  • Two routes attack one defender at different leverage/depth.
  • QB reads defender, not favorite receiver.
  • Rotate defender role so all players learn the conflict.

H. Continuous 3v3

  • Three-play possessions, immediate change of direction after turnover/score.
  • 30-45 second rest between mini-series.
  • Conditioning comes from football movement.

Coach Roles

Head CoachQB/offense · opening message · offensive install · situational periods · play calling
Assistant 1Defense · flag pulling · coverage · rushers · pursuit · defensive calls
Assistant 2Skills/operations · catching · centers/snaps · cones · timing · attendance · rotations
Player Growth System

Player Development & Evaluation

A season-long measurement system for all 10 players: baseline testing, QB competition, skill evaluation, attendance, game reps, depth-chart development, and end-of-season improvement.

TEST Baseline + RetestGRADE 1–5 Skill ScaleTRACK Attendance + Game RepsPLAN Individual Goals

Development Dashboard

The workbook is designed to answer one question at the end of the winter: Did each player become a better all-around football player? Use the baseline in Week 1, coach throughout the season, and repeat the same measures at the end.

Initial QB Candidates

Player Profile

Primary and developmental positions, jersey number, status, parent contact, and the one development priority that matters most.

Attendance

Track all 27 preseason sessions using Present, Absent, Excused, and Injured codes so opportunity and development can be viewed in context.

Athletic Baseline

10-yard, 20-yard, 40-yard, 5-10-5, broad jump, 7-yard rush, catching percentage, throwing accuracy, and throwing distance.

Football Skills

Baseline and final ratings for hands, routes, ball security, speed, agility, football IQ, flag pulling, coverage, rush, and leadership.

QB Competition

Weighted evaluation for accuracy, decision-making, anticipation, footwork, mobility, communication/leadership, and arm strength.

Depth Chart

Primary and secondary offensive/defensive roles, package assignments, rotation notes, and developmental backups.

Game Reps

Track offensive and defensive snaps, targets, receptions, passing reps, touchdowns, flag pulls, missed flags, and pressures.

Individual Plans

Set a primary goal, secondary goal, weekly drill focus, optional home assignment, and progress notes for every player.

Coach Scoring Standard

Use the same 1–5 scale across the staff so improvement means the same thing regardless of who is grading.

1Not Yet
2Developing
3Functional
4Strong
5Game-Changing

QB Competition Framework

CategoryWeightWhat We Are Looking For
Accuracy25%Catchable placement, especially short/intermediate throws
Decision-Making20%Correct defender read, progression discipline, turnover avoidance
Anticipation / Timing15%Ball out before the receiver is fully open; rhythm under the 7-second clock
Footwork / Mechanics15%Balanced base, repeatable release, efficient movement
Mobility10%Escapes space, resets, throws on movement without panic
Communication / Leadership10%Huddle command, formation correction, composure, teammate communication
Arm Strength5%Enough velocity and range to access the full offense

Development rule: height is not scored. We are selecting and developing the quarterback who best operates the offense, not the player who simply looks most like a tackle-football quarterback.

Testing & Retest Plan

Week 1 Baseline

Capture athletic testing, catching/throwing measures, coach skill grades, and initial position projections before the system shapes player roles.

Weekly Coaching

Use practice attendance, individual-plan notes, depth-chart reps, and game data to drive the next week's coaching focus.

End-of-Season Retest

Repeat the same measurable tests and coach evaluations. Compare like-for-like rather than changing the test because a player improved.

Excel Development Workbook

Use the full workbook for live player data, formulas, attendance, QB rankings, game reps, and individual development plans.
